title: Heat Pump Vs. Furnace - Which is BETTER?
summary: A Texas HVAC contractor compares gas, heat pump and dual-fuel systems on comfort, install cost, savings and lifespan, estimating a heat pump repays its extra cost in about five years, or at once with the $2,000 credit.

assertions.quote: for upfront cost the furnace is going to be the cheapest the heat pump is going to be the most expensive
you're going to need to add a couple Breakers at the pan panel and run new electrical wiring to the indoor unit
heat pumps are more energy efficient than gas systems and should be able to save you $300 to $500 in energy cost each year
the increased cost to convert a gas system to a heat pump could be offset in savings by year five
the federal tax credit for qualified heat pump systems offers around $2,000 in tax credits
for dual fuel it's going to be closer to $5,000
it would essentially be air conditioning your house for about 5 minutes and would melt all the frost off the outdoor unit
in freezing temperatures the heat pump is going to struggle some
it both Heats and cools so that means it runs year round so it ends up wearing out a little bit faster

verdicts.note: Heat pumps typically last 12-15 years, similar to central ACs but shorter than many gas furnaces.

assertions.quote: we can clearly see that a gas system gets quite a bit hotter than a heat pump

verdicts.note: Heat pumps have lower supply air temperatures than furnaces, so duct sealing is recommended to keep the air supplied to rooms comfortable.
Heat pump supply air rarely exceeded 100F (often around 80F) versus about 120F for fossil furnaces; occupant comfort was not measured.

Units that kept the fan on without auxiliary heat during defrost blew air averaging below 60 F, yet no occupant complained of it; it is a defrost-period effect, not a general comparison with furnace supply air.

assertions.quote: a small generator can easily power a furnace

verdicts.note: A gas furnace's blower draws a few hundred watts, while a heat pump with strip heat needs several kilowatts at 240V.
